facts.text: Independent bookshop in the Queens Village neighborhood of South Philadelphia.
Run by co-owners Noelle Egan and Patrick Richardson Graham.
Hosts music events and poetry readings.
Flyers-themed sports bar inside Stateside Live (formerly Xfinity Live!) in the South Philadelphia sports complex.
Displays memorabilia from the Flyers' Broad Street Bullies era.
Irish pub in the Old City neighborhood.
Opened in 2013 as one of the first modern German beer halls in Philadelphia.
Serves German, Belgian and American beers alongside bratwursts and pretzels.
Has self-serve draft taps where guests pour their own beer with a Haus Key.
Two-floor, 8,000 square foot bar in the Old City section of Philadelphia.
Has Brunswick pool tables, shuffleboard tables, dart boards, Pop-A-Shot, Buck Hunter and pinball.
Offers private room rentals for groups of up to 242 guests.
Bar inside Gather Food Hall at Schuylkill Yards, 3025 Market Street.
Serves steaks, burgers and comfort food, including The Trough and a 50oz Tomahawk steak.
Butchery-inspired dining space with 16 beers on tap, draft wines and a whiskey-based cocktail program.
Small business in downtown Narberth that appraises and purchases antiques and precious metals.
Buys coins, jewelry, watches, military items, artwork and flatware.
Outdoor beer garden beside the canal in Manayunk, with waterside views.
Serves cocktails, craft beers and wines.
Waterfront beer garden, bar, restaurant and nightclub.
Large outdoor deck on the water with the Ben Franklin Bridge as a backdrop.
Features rotating weekly DJs.
Held along Cecil B. Moore Avenue between Broad and 13th Streets.
Accepts EBT, WIC and senior FMNP vouchers and Philly Food Bucks.
Sits at 22nd and Cherry Streets in the Logan Square neighborhood; it was previously Dever's Bar.
During Prohibition the bar was removed and the space became a barber shop.
Bought in 1972 by John "Tex" Flannery, who sold it to brothers Bill and Bob Loughery in 1990.
Flagship location of the chain, in the South Philadelphia Stadium District on Packer Avenue.
Sits on the corner of Shurs Lane and Pechin Street, a few blocks off Manayunk's Main Street.
Pours 12 rotating draft beers and has 21 flat screen TVs for sports.
Menu includes wings and Eck's-treme fries.
Opened in March 2016 with a modern twist on the Philly cheesesteak.
Sandwiches use 100% USDA domestic ribeye, and the owners have run a cheesesteak manufacturing company for over 40 years.
West Philadelphia shop for records, music supplies, used gear and instrument and electronics repair.
Buys used records and musician gear and rents Technics 1200 turntables.
Created by Limerick men Liam Kelly and Maurice Collins with help from Irish craftsmen.
Named as a tribute to an old friend from Ireland, Con Murphy.
Located at the Windsor Suites, with one bar on the main level and another on the second floor.
Serves cocktails and craft beers.
Hosts live music on Friday and Saturday nights.
Opened in the former Yards Brewing Co. building at 901 N. Delaware Ave, vacant since late 2017.
About 35,000 square feet with a bakery, two bars, a music stage and a playground for kids and adults.
Concept came from Avram Hornik; beer is brewed by Mainstay Independent under Brian O'Reilly.
Record shop and independent label that sells its own releases and exclusive pressings.
Also has a second record store location in West Chester, PA.
